cohort: 1,796 pregnant Chinese women with singleton pregnancies
finding: Childbirth self-efficacy was found to be low among pregnant Chinese women, with younger age, lower BMI, receiving prenatal education, frequent physical activity, and good self-rated health being significantly associated with higher childbirth self-efficacy.
mod_finding: This study investigated factors influencing childbirth self-efficacy among pregnant Chinese women, including their preferred mode of delivery, but did not specifically analyze findings related to mode of delivery.
